summary: Track 08 (EU AI Act Art.10 mapping) open-flags resolution: regulatory-tag lookup-table workaround (no MetricResult schema change), Art.10(5)-to-Art.4a relocation under the Digital Omnibus (in force 27 Jul 2026) with draft legal-basis paragraph, and Annex IV §5/§9 scope-boundary text.
result_text:
# Track 08 — Open Flags Resolution

Resolves the three items flagged as open in Track 08 (EU AI Act Article 10 mapping). One new finding surfaced during this pass that changes Flag 2's substance.

---

## Flag 1 — Regulatory tagging on `MetricResult` (schema-lock conflict)

Non-invasive workaround, no `MetricResult` field added — M1 schema lock stays intact:

```python
# report/regulatory_tags.py (proposed — NOT part of schema.py)
from bias_aperture.schema import MetricResult
from collections.abc import Iterable

REGULATORY_TAG_MAP: dict[str, list[str]] = {
    "demographic_parity_difference": ["Art.10(2)(f)", "Art.10(2)(g)", "NIST-MEASURE-2.11"],
    "equalized_odds_difference":     ["Art.10(2)(f)", "Art.10(2)(g)", "NIST-MEASURE-2.11"],
    "equal_opportunity_difference":  ["Art.10(2)(f)", "Art.10(2)(g)", "NIST-MEASURE-2.11"],
    "disparate_impact_ratio":        ["Art.10(2)(f)", "Art.10(2)(g)", "NIST-MEASURE-2.11"],
}

def tag_rows(results: Iterable[MetricResult]) -> list[dict]:
    """Join at report-generation time only; MetricResult itself untouched."""
    return [{"result": r, "regulatory_tags": REGULATORY_TAG_MAP[r.metric_name]} for r in results]
```

The report template consumes this joined dict, never `MetricResult` directly — FR-003/FR-004's locked shape is unaffected.

**Decision needed from Stream A/B:** keep this as a permanent lookup table (recommended — it's a pure function of the already-closed `metric_name` enum, so it can't drift out of sync with the schema) vs. promoting to a real `MetricResult` field at a future milestone (only worth revisiting if tagging ever needs to vary *per subgroup* rather than per metric_name — not the case today, since Art.10(2)(f)/(g) apply uniformly to all four bias metrics).

---

## Flag 2 — Article 10(5) legal-basis statement (superseded by a regulatory change)

**New finding, not in the original Track 08 output:** Article 10(5) has been deleted from Article 10 and its content relocated to a new **Article 4a** ("Processing of special categories of personal data for bias detection and correction"), in force **27 July 2026**, under the EU's Digital Omnibus — the first amendment package to the AI Act since its 2024 adoption (Council/Parliament provisional agreement 7 May 2026; Parliament vote 16 June 2026). Confirmed against the official amended text on artificialintelligenceact.eu (track-changes view shows all of old Art.10(5)(a)-(f) marked "not present after the amendment," with equivalent content appearing as new Art.4a(1)(a)-(f)).

What's substantively the same vs. new:

- **Same:** the five conditions (no adequate substitute incl. synthetic/anonymised data; technical/pseudonymisation safeguards; access controls with documentation; no third-party transfer; deletion on completion or retention-end) plus the RoPA necessity-documentation requirement — these map close to 1:1 onto old Art.10(5)(a)-(f).
- **Changed:** the citation. Old `Art.10(5)` → new `Art.4a(1)`, now explicitly invoked "in accordance with Article 10(2), points (f) and (g)" — which ties Art.4a eligibility directly to the same DPD/EOD/EOP/DIR-to-Art.10(2) mapping Track 08 already produced.
- **New:** Art.4a(2) expands the exception beyond high-risk-system *providers* to also cover *deployers* of high-risk systems and providers/deployers of non-high-risk systems, under the same five conditions. Art.4a(2) also states explicitly that it "does not create any obligation to conduct such bias detection and correction" — worth noting as a scope clarification.

**Draft legal-basis paragraph** (for Stream A/B to adopt or revise):

> BiasAperture's demographic schema (`race`, `gender`, `age`; `schema.py`) constitutes special-category personal data under GDPR Art.9(1). Processing this data to compute the Core Four fairness metrics is permitted under EU AI Act Art.4a(1) (introduced by the Digital Omnibus, in force 27 July 2026; formerly Art.10(5)), to the extent strictly necessary to fulfil the Art.10(2)(f)-(g) bias-examination duties, subject to the five Art.4a(1)(a)-(f) conditions. BiasAperture operates on the public FairFace benchmark rather than deployer-collected personal data; this statement documents the applicable legal basis for completeness of the regulatory-mapping deliverable, not because BiasAperture itself performs GDPR-regulated processing of a live subject population.

**Ownership: still unresolved.** The renumbering doesn't close the original gap — no track in the 20-track division owns drafting/approving this paragraph for the final report. It's now a short approval decision rather than open research; recommend Stream A/B assign it directly.

---

## Flag 3 — Annex IV §5/§9 scope boundary

Confirmed: §5 = risk-management-system documentation per Art.9 (risk identification, analysis, mitigation, residual-risk sign-off, as a continuous process); §9 = post-market-monitoring-plan documentation per Art.72(3) (real-world performance tracking, degradation detection, incident reporting).

**Draft boundary paragraph** (for the report's regulatory-mapping section):

> This report's regulatory mapping is scoped to Article 10 (Data and Data Governance) and its intersection with BiasAperture's four Core Four fairness metrics. Annex IV §5 (risk-management-system documentation, Art.9) and §9 (post-market-monitoring-plan documentation, Art.72) fall outside this scope: BiasAperture is a point-in-time diagnostic audit tool, not a deployed system requiring an ongoing risk-management process or post-market monitoring plan. A provider adopting BiasAperture within a compliance pipeline would need to supply §5/§9 documentation separately — informed by, but not generated by, BiasAperture's metric output. This is a deliberate scope boundary, not an omission.

---

## Summary — actions needed from Stream A/B

1. Approve or revise the regulatory-tag lookup table (Flag 1) — no schema change required.
2. Approve/assign ownership of the Art.4a legal-basis paragraph (Flag 2) for the final report.
3. Confirm the Annex IV §5/§9 boundary paragraph (Flag 3), verbatim or revised.
4. **New action item surfaced here:** Track 08's original Article 10 mapping predates the Digital Omnibus and doesn't reference Art.4a. Recommend a short addendum to Track 08's existing deliverable (not a rewrite) noting the Art.10(5)→Art.4a relocation, so final-report citations are current as of the 27 July 2026 amendment.

**Sources:** artificialintelligenceact.eu — Article 10 (official amended text, track-changes view); Article 4a (official text, in force 27 July 2026); Digital Omnibus overview. Council of the EU press release, 7 May 2026 (provisional agreement). Cross-checked against euaiact.com and Deeploy/Warden AI secondary analyses for consistency.
